content:
The image shows a leaf with a large, dark brown to reddish-purple necrotic lesion occupying a significant portion of the leaf, particularly at or near the leaf margin/tip. The surrounding tissue shows yellowing/chlorotic coloration transitioning from healthy green to diseased tissue.

**Key visual features:**
- Large, irregular dark brown/purplish-brown necrotic patch
- Lesion located at the leaf edge/margin area
- Surrounding tissue shows yellowish coloration
- No circular spots with distinct grey centers and dark rings (ruling out Brown_Eye_Spot/Berry_Blotch)
- No pale yellow trails or mines under the epidermis (ruling out Miner)
- No orange/yellow powdery spore masses visible (ruling out Rust)
- No small circular patterns — the lesion is large and irregular

**Matching to Phoma:** The description states "circular dark-colored spots of varying sizes on leaves up to 2 cm diameter; infection begins at the apical part in the terminal shoot and tender leaves; leaves curve and may present cracks when lesions reach edges." The dark, large, irregular necrotic area starting from the leaf margin/tip is most consistent with Phoma infection.
